Exact-Null Max-Calibrated Shrinkage When p Is Much Larger Than n

Source: vignettes/HDMaxShrink.Rmd
HDMaxShrink.Rmd

~{r, include = FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = “#>”)~

HDMaxShrink considers

y=X_A\beta_A+X_B\beta_B+\varepsilon, \qquad H_0:\beta_B=0,

where p_1=|A|<n, p=p_1+q may greatly exceed n, and the tested block may itself satisfy q>n. The partition must be prespecified independently of the response used for inference.

Independently selected CPSS core

Version 0.6.2 preserves the version 0.6.1 statistical API and uses singleton-group grpreg MCP for the optional CPSS–MCP sensitivity path. Version 0.6.1 added portable linkage for the compiled numerical kernels. The version 0.6.0 workflow can learn an optional extension to a mandatory core on an independent selection sample using complementary-pairs stability selection (CPSS):

~~~{r, eval = FALSE} selection <- cpss_select_core( X_selection, y_selection, selector = “lasso”, complementary_pairs = 50, base_selection_size = 20, stability_threshold = 0.60, seed = 20260825, mandatory_core = c(“lineage_2”, “lineage_3”, “MSIScore”), candidate_set = grep(“^expr::”, colnames(X_selection)) )

fit <- fit_cpss_ridge_shrinkage( X_analysis, y_analysis, selection = selection, ridge_lambda = 0.25, bootstrap_B = 999, bootstrap_seed = 20260826 ) ~~~

Within every complementary half-sample, the mandatory design is centered and projected out by an economy SVD before LASSO or MCP is fitted to the optional candidate family. Mandatory variables are not CPSS discoveries and do not enter the CPSS PFER denominator. The final core is the union of the mandatory set and the thresholded CPSS extension; an empty extension leaves the mandatory core unchanged without a top-k fallback.

This defines the CPSS-guided exact-null submodel

\widehat\beta^{CPSS\text{-}SM}_{\widehat A} =(X_{\widehat A}^{s})^+y^s, \qquad \widehat\beta^{CPSS\text{-}SM}_{\widehat A^c}=0,

and an all-X direct dual-Ridge FM. The max-partial-t test is computed from the exact-null SM residual rather than from Ridge. CPSS is due to Shah and Samworth (2013); the package contribution is the CPSS–SM/Ridge/max-shrinkage composition, not CPSS itself. CPSS–LASSO is the primary selector and CPSS–MCP is a sensitivity selector. Singleton groups make its group MCP penalty the ordinary coordinatewise MCP penalty. Because grpreg does not expose a local-convexity index, the compatibility field is NA and no local-convexity claim is made. Selection and analysis samples must be independent for the conditional test argument. A threshold at or below one half is only an exploratory frequency screen and carries no PFER claim.

Full and submodel estimators

Within each training fit, center and RMS-scale every retained predictor and the response:

X^s_{ij}=\frac{X_{ij}-\bar X_j}{s_j},\qquad y_i^s=\frac{y_i-\bar y}{s_y}.

The primary FM estimator is one joint all-X square-root LASSO:

\widehat b^{FM}\in\arg\min_{b\in\mathbb R^p} \left\{\frac{\|y^s-X^sb\|_2}{\sqrt n} +\lambda\sum_{j=1}^p\omega_j|b_j|\right\},\qquad \omega_j>0.

Every one of the p coefficients is estimated and penalized in this single optimization. The standardized intercept is exactly zero. Coefficients are returned on the original scale as \widehat\beta_j=s_y\widehat b_j/s_j, with original-scale intercept \bar y-\bar X^\top\widehat\beta.

The fresh submodel refit under the null is

\widehat b^{SM}=((X_A^s)^+y^s,0_q).

This is a genuine restricted refit: its core coordinates generally differ from those of FM. It is not obtained by copying the FM core, and no true active set is provided. The implementation computes X_A^+ from an economy SVD after checking numerical rank. It never assumes that an OLS Gram inverse exists.

High-dimensional maximum test

The all-X FM optimization does not determine the null-test statistic. The test starts from the exact-null residual. Let

M_A=I-X_A^s(X_A^s)^+,\qquad d=n-1-\operatorname{rank}(X_A^s),\qquad z_j=M_AX^s_{B,j},\qquad r_0=M_Ay^s,

and define

T_{\mathrm{score}} =\max_{j\in B} \frac{|z_j^\top r_0|} {\|z_j\|_2\sqrt{\|r_0\|_2^2/d}}, \qquad T_{\max,t}=\sqrt{ \frac{(d-1)T_{\mathrm{score}}^2} {d-T_{\mathrm{score}}^2}}.

Under the exact null, homoskedastic Gaussian errors, and a prespecified core, Gaussian draws are centered and projected off the same core. Applying the same monotone transform to the observed and simulated maxima leaves the Monte Carlo p-value and PT decision unchanged. This is conditional Gaussian Monte Carlo calibration, not a residual multiplier bootstrap. No direct chi-square limit, joint F(q,d-1) law, or q\times q covariance inversion is used. Put

\widehat\kappa= \left\{B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B (T_{\max,t}^{*(b)})^{-2}\right\}^{-1}.

The resulting positive-part estimator is

\widehat\beta^{PS} =\widehat\beta^{SM} +\left[1-\frac{\widehat\kappa} {T_{\max,t}^2\vee\epsilon}\right]_+ (\widehat\beta^{FM}-\widehat\beta^{SM}).

The untruncated Stein and preliminary-test variants are returned as S and PT. Classical James–Stein dominance is not asserted for the max calibration.

Reproducible template

~~~{r, eval = FALSE} set.seed(20260820) n <- 100 p <- 1000 p1 <- 20 X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p) beta <- numeric(p) core_pattern <- c( 1.50, 1.25, 1.00, 0.90, 0.80, -1.25, -1.00, -0.90, 0.75, -0.75 ) beta[1:20] <- rep(core_pattern, 2) y <- drop(X %*% beta + rnorm(n))

fit <- fit_partial_sqrt_lasso_shrinkage( X, y, core_set = 1:p1, tested_set = (p1 + 1):p, full_endpoint = “all_x_square_root_lasso”, all_x_penalty_loadings = rep(1, p), standardize_y = TRUE, bootstrap_B = 499, bootstrap_seed = 20260820 )

print(fit) coef(fit, method = “FM”) coef(fit, method = “SM”) coef(fit, method = “PT”) coef(fit, method = “S”) coef(fit, method = “PS”) ~~~

Here all 20 coordinates in the prespecified core are active. Under the exact null, SM is the intended correct-restriction benchmark; its construction uses the prespecified partition, not a separately supplied true-support vector.

The all-X FM endpoint does not require diagonal population precision. Conditional on a fixed design, the exact-null test does not itself require independent design columns, but its finite-sample exactness does require the prespecified core and iid homoskedastic Gaussian errors under the null.

Simulation risk

The paper simulation uses the full coefficient loss

\|\widehat\beta-\beta\|_2^2,

and reports

\operatorname{RPE}(m)= \frac{\operatorname{MSE}(FM)}{\operatorname{MSE}(m)}.

This convention makes the exact-null SM curve tend toward zero under large \Delta=\|\beta_B\|_2. When T_{\max} diverges, the S and PS weights approach one, the estimators approach FM, and their RPE approaches one.

Retained modes

The package still contains fit_ridge_mcp_shrinkage() and the earlier fit_hd_shrinkage() projection/Wald implementation. They are retained for sensitivity analysis and reproducibility. The thresholded partial-debiased and profiled partial square-root-LASSO endpoints also remain explicit options. They remain available alongside the version 0.5.0 CPSS–SM/Ridge extension.

  • Shah, R. D. and Samworth, R. J. (2013). Variable selection with error control: another look at stability selection. JRSS B, 75, 55–80. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.01034.x.
  • Belloni, A. and Chernozhukov, V. (2013). Least squares after model selection in high-dimensional sparse models. Bernoulli, 19, 521–547. doi:10.3150/11-BEJ410.
  • Dufour, J.-M. (2006). Monte Carlo tests with nuisance parameters. Journal of Econometrics, 133, 443–477. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.06.007.
